findings.summary: hestia.rs is listed as an expected deliverable, but the plan leaves it unchanged so the diff stays within criterion 5's three files. If the verifier checks deliverables against the diff, it may flag this.
findings.evidence: The brief lists crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (modify) under Expected deliverables. Criterion 5 says the diff touches only docs/spec.toml, status.rs and CHANGELOG.md. measure_problem (hestia.rs:1219-1239) reads crate::status::STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS by reference, so no logic edit is needed there. Fix: Keep the three-file diff: the criteria outrank the deliverables list. Have the producer's report say explicitly that hestia.rs is not modified, why, and which hestia tests ran (`cargo test -p athena-core --lib hestia`), so the verifier does not read it as a missing deliverable.
findings.location: Plan Decision 1 / Risks (hestia.rs deliverable) vs Expected deliverables

findings.summary: The mechanism says Manager::restart records each restart 'of the person acting for Athena'. The code's own doc comment says 'a restart of the user's own context'. Nothing in the code ties the record to the person acting for Athena.
findings.evidence: manage.rs:443 reads `/// \`athena restart\`: records a restart of the user's own context.` RestartArgs (manage.rs:49-56) has cost, minutes, tokens, measured, lost and via, so the 'what it cost and what was lost' part is accurate. Fix: Word the mechanism as 'records each restart (its cost and what was lost)', or say it is a restart of the acting context. Don't claim more identity than the record holds.

findings.summary: Showing the test fails on the base is optional ('Optionally comment out the table row'), but criterion 3 requires that the test fails on the base tree.
findings.evidence: Criterion 3 says 'The test fails on the base tree (label rejected) and passes now'. Step 5 makes the check optional, and Risks says the claim rests on reading the code. Fix: Make it a required step: remove the row, run `cargo test -p athena-core --lib oly_b_o5_01`, record the failure message (the `restarts`-not-printed message, from part (a)), restore the row, and rerun until it passes. Report both outputs.

summary: I read the code, and the plan's claims about it hold. STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS (status.rs:305-322) has no restarts row today. measure_problem (hestia.rs:1219-1239) rejects any label not in that table. display.rs:1411 prints `restarts    {}`, which satisfies every_measure_label_names_a_status_view_field_and_a_printed_line (status.rs:1659-1678). StatusView already has the `restarts` field. OLY-B-O5-01 (spec.toml:2265-2268) has mechanism "none" and measure `status: requirement`. Manager::restart exists at manage.rs:444. So the fix starts where the fault is, in the one table row, and the spec entry is updated to use it. The new test copies the existing OLY-B-GOAL-03 real-spec test (status.rs:1630-1656). It calls the real parse_spec, measure_problem and spec_gaps on the real docs/spec.toml through include_str!, and its label assertion fails on the base tree, which answers the prior job's review findings. The xtask checker (xtask/tests/spec.rs:194-213) only needs a non-empty label, so it passes. The only other readers of STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS are the hestia doc comment and the spec.toml header comment; neither needs an edit, and the dependents list covers the code readers. SPEED_LABELS correctly stays unchanged. I found no soundness problem: the approach is an exact-string table entry, not a heuristic. The three minor findings: the hestia.rs deliverable mismatch should be explained in the producer's report; the mechanism wording overstates who the restart record belongs to; and the fails-on-base run should be required, not optional.
